AppleAuthRequest.description:
Sign in with Apple identity-token exchange.

``nonce`` is required (unlike the Google mobile path): the iOS client
always embeds its generated nonce verbatim in the identity token, so the
server can bind the token to this request and reject replays.
AppleAuthRequest.title: AppleAuthRequest

AuthTokenResponse.description:
Response for register / login / verify-email / google.

When ``status == "verification_required"`` (returned by /register when the
server enforces verification), ``access_token`` is ``None`` and the client
must call /verify-email with the code from the OTP email to obtain the JWT.
For all other ``status`` values (currently just ``"ok"``) a valid
``access_token`` is always present.

``scheduled_deletion_at`` (ISO-8601, UTC) is non-null when the account is
in the soft-delete grace window — clients surface a "cancel scheduled
deletion" banner so the user can restore the account.

``refresh_token`` and ``expires_in`` are non-null only when the request
asked for a refreshable session (see ``RefreshableSessionRequest``). This
is also the response of ``POST /api/auth/refresh``, where ``status`` is
always ``"ok"``.
AuthTokenResponse.title: AuthTokenResponse

CreateAgentResponse.description: Returned once on creation — includes raw token.
CreateAgentResponse.title: CreateAgentResponse

CustomAgentTypeSummary.description: Wire shape for a custom agent type returned to clients.
CustomAgentTypeSummary.title: CustomAgentTypeSummary

DeleteAccountRequest.description:
Re-auth proof for ``POST /api/auth/me/delete``.

The client must supply ONE of:
  * ``method="password"`` with a non-empty ``password`` (password users)
  * ``method="google"`` with a fresh ``id_token`` + the ``nonce`` the
    client used when obtaining it (Google-OAuth users)
  * ``method="apple"`` with a fresh ``id_token`` + ``nonce`` (Sign in
    with Apple users)

``mode`` chooses between the soft-delete grace window (``scheduled``,
default — 14 days, cancellable) and an irreversible cascade purge
(``immediate``). Omitting ``mode`` preserves the legacy behavior for
older clients.

Existing session JWT alone is rejected — re-auth is a hard requirement
for self-delete (Auth0 / Google Identity guidance).
DeleteAccountRequest.title: DeleteAccountRequest

DeviceCodeConfirmRequest.description:
Browser's approval of a redeemed code.

Carries the same device fields as ``PairingClaimRequest`` because the
confirm runs the identical completion path.
DeviceCodeConfirmRequest.title: DeviceCodeConfirmRequest

DeviceCodeMintResponse.description:
Server's reply to ``POST /api/pairing/device-code``.

``request_id`` is the handle every follow-up call uses, so the code
itself never travels in a URL path or query string where the relay's
access log would capture it.
DeviceCodeMintResponse.title: DeviceCodeMintResponse

DeviceCodeRedeemRequest.description:
The agent's anonymous redeem, keyed by the retyped code.

``redeemer_id`` is generated and persisted by the agent *before* the
request goes out. The nonce is handed out exactly once, so without a
stable redeemer identity a response lost in transit would leave the
operator holding a burnt code and no way to reach the pairing
WebSocket; a retry carrying the same id is answered from the existing
row instead of rejected as a double redeem.
DeviceCodeRedeemRequest.title: DeviceCodeRedeemRequest

DeviceCodeRedeemResponse.description:
What the agent needs to wait for its credentials.

Shaped like ``PairingInitiateResponse`` minus the QR text: the agent
derives the WS URL from ``RELAY_SERVER_URL`` + ``nonce`` exactly as it
does for the QR flow.

``account_hint`` is a masked address, and it is the load-bearing
control of the reversed direction. Because the browser mints the code,
a confirmation shown only in the browser is confirmed by whoever minted
it — including an attacker who talked the operator into running the
command. Naming the account on the agent's own terminal is what lets
the human refuse.

``nonce`` is ``None`` on a replayed redeem: it is never stored
server-side, so a retrying agent reads it back from its own pending
file.
DeviceCodeRedeemResponse.title: DeviceCodeRedeemResponse

DeviceCodeStatusResponse.description:
Poll state for the browser half of the flow.

``hostname`` / ``os`` come from the anonymous redeem body and are
therefore attacker-settable — the same caveat that applies to the QR
flow's ``current_agent_id``. They are shown so a legitimate operator
can recognise their machine, not as an authentication signal.

``blocked_reason`` surfaces the ownership verdict *before* the confirm
click, so a re-pair that is going to 404 or 409 says so while the code
and nonce are still spendable.

``repair_agent_name`` is set only when the redeeming host claims an
agent this account already owns. Approving then *moves* that agent —
rotating its token onto the redeemer and knocking the real host
offline — so the clients must name it rather than asking the
first-pair question.
DeviceCodeStatusResponse.title: DeviceCodeStatusResponse

DeviceResponse.description:
One entry in the user's ``GET /api/devices`` listing.

``platform`` is the free-form label the device sent when it last minted
agent tokens (``"ios"``, ``"android"``, ``"web"``); it is null for rows
registered by a client that omitted the field.
DeviceResponse.title: DeviceResponse

MobileTokenRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/token``.

The mobile client identifies the *device* asking for tokens. The
``user_id`` is taken from the dashboard JWT in the Authorization
header. ``mobile_device_name`` is an auto-generated label like
``"Google Pixel 8"`` that the user sees on the "My devices" screen.

``mobile_device_id`` is constrained to a canonical 36-char UUID
string (defence in depth: narrows the attack surface for
cross-tenant collisions and prevents convenient short literals like
``"admin"``).
MobileTokenRequest.title: MobileTokenRequest

PairingClaimRequest.description:
Mobile's claim request (authenticated).

``mobile_device_id`` is constrained to a canonical 36-char UUID
string — same defence-in-depth check as ``MobileTokenRequest``.
PairingClaimRequest.title: PairingClaimRequest

PairingClaimResponse.description:
Server's reply to a successful claim — no token reaches the mobile.

``ws_delivered`` is a diagnostic hint, not an authority signal. ``True``
means the credential push was dispatched directly to the agent's pairing
WebSocket (the agent was connected at claim time); ``False`` means the
push was staged in the server-side recovery slot for the agent's next
WS reconnect to consume. The mobile uses this to refine the timeout-error
copy when the agent does not subsequently come online — it does NOT
treat ``True`` as "the agent is now paired" (the agent could still fail
to validate the signature, fail to write ``.env``, or fail to start its
relay client; only the routing-table ``agent.status_changed=true``
event is authoritative).
PairingClaimResponse.title: PairingClaimResponse

PairingInitiateRequest.description:
Optional metadata the agent reports at initiate time.

All fields are advisory: the mobile UI uses ``hostname`` / ``os`` to
let the operator confirm they're claiming the right host;
``current_agent_id`` distinguishes a re-pair (token rotation for the
same owner) from a first-pair (new ``agents`` row at claim). A claim by
a different account is rejected — ownership is not transferable by
pairing.
PairingInitiateRequest.title: PairingInitiateRequest

PairingInitiateResponse.description:
Server's reply to ``POST /api/pairing/initiate``.

``qr_payload`` is the canonical ``MOBA1|...`` text the agent renders.
``trust_key_fp`` is the SHA-256 fingerprint of the server's manifest
signing public key — the agent cross-checks this against its own
pinned key before trusting the flow. The pairing WS URL is *not*
returned: the agent derives it locally from ``RELAY_SERVER_URL`` +
``nonce`` so a deployment-skewed server cannot hand back a buggy
scheme (``https://...``) that the websockets client would reject.
PairingInitiateResponse.title: PairingInitiateResponse

ReregisterAgentResponse.description: Returned on credential rotation — includes new raw token.
ReregisterAgentResponse.title: ReregisterAgentResponse

ShortcutSummary.description: Wire shape for a saved shortcut returned to clients.
ShortcutSummary.title: ShortcutSummary

TemplateSummary.description: Wire shape for a prompt template returned to clients.
TemplateSummary.title: TemplateSummary

TrustPinResponse.description:
The relay's current signing fingerprint and the account's pin.

Read-only and advisory. Clients display it and may warn on a
difference; they must NOT write it into their local trust store.
TrustPinResponse.title: TrustPinResponse

UpdateCustomAgentTypeRequest.description:
Partial update: omitted/null fields stay unchanged. Unlike shortcut
names, ``name`` and ``command`` are mandatory attributes of a type, so
there is no empty-string-clears form — a provided-but-blank value is a
validation error, and an empty body is rejected outright.
UpdateCustomAgentTypeRequest.title: UpdateCustomAgentTypeRequest

UpdateShortcutRequest.description:
Rename-only update. ``name`` is required so an empty body cannot
silently clear it; ``""`` (or an explicit null) clears the name back to
NULL — the Android client's JSON encoder omits null-valued defaults, so
the empty string is the only clear form it can express on the wire.
UpdateShortcutRequest.title: UpdateShortcutRequest

UpdateTemplateRequest.description:
Partial update — every field is optional. The router rejects an
all-None payload at the service layer.
UpdateTemplateRequest.title: UpdateTemplateRequest

UserRefreshRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/auth/refresh``.

Unauthenticated by design — the refresh token *is* the credential, so
presenting a dead access token alongside it must not matter.
UserRefreshRequest.title: UserRefreshRequest

get.description: List agents owned by the authenticated user, with online status.

schema.title: Response List Agents Api Agents Get

post.description: Create a new agent owned by the authenticated user. Returns credentials once.

delete.description: Delete an agent and cascade all related data. Owner only.

post.description: Regenerate agent credentials. Owner only.

Get mobile access + refresh tokens for an agent the user owns.

The mobile client supplies its per-install ``mobile_device_id`` so the
issued JWT's ``sub`` claim and the refresh-token row are scoped to
that specific device, not to the user account.
Authenticate via Apple identity token (Sign in with Apple on iOS).
Send a password-reset OTP by email. Always returns 200 to defeat enumeration.
Authenticate via Google ID token (from Android Credential Manager).
Authenticate a user with email + password.

Schedule or immediately purge the calling user's account.

``body.mode`` chooses between ``'scheduled'`` (default — 14-day soft-delete
with a cancel link) and ``'immediate'`` (irreversible cascade purge now).
Older clients that omit ``mode`` get the legacy scheduled behavior.

Requires a fresh credential proof (current password OR fresh Google ID
token with matching nonce) — the session JWT alone is rejected. On
success: writes the audit row, revokes refresh tokens, closes any live
user/agent WebSockets with code 4010, and (scheduled mode only) emails a
single-use cancel link before returning 204.

Refuses to act on the seed-admin account (mirrors the admin-path guard).

Restore an account that is currently in the soft-delete grace window.

Idempotent: succeeds even if no deletion was scheduled. The previous
``scheduled_deletion_at`` (or None) is echoed back so the client can
confirm what was cancelled.

Rotate a user-session refresh token into a fresh access token.

Unauthenticated by design: the refresh token is the credential, and the
access token this call replaces has usually already expired. The
presented refresh token is consumed, so a replay returns 401 — clients
must serialize concurrent refreshes rather than racing them.

Register a new user with email + password.

When email verification is required, the response has
``status="verification_required"`` and ``access_token=None``; the client
must call ``/api/auth/verify-email`` with the code from the OTP email.
Issue a fresh verification code (rate-limited).
Consume a reset OTP and replace the user's password.
Consume a verification code and return the JWT.

get.description: List the caller's non-deleted custom agent types.

schema.title: Response List Custom Agent Types Api Custom Agent Types Get

delete.description: Soft-delete the type and (server-side) its kind-scoped shortcuts.

get.description: Return the authenticated user's non-revoked devices.

schema.title: Response List Devices Api Devices Get

delete.description:
Revoke one of the authenticated user's devices.

Idempotency / safety: returns 404 if the device does not belong to the
user (or was already revoked). On success, also invalidates every
outstanding refresh token bound to that device across all agents — the
revoked device fails on its next ``/api/mobile/refresh`` round-trip
and signs out, while the user's other devices stay logged in.

Clear the push token for one of the caller's devices (sign-out path).

Idempotent for an owned device with no stored token; 404 when the device
does not belong to the caller or is revoked.

post.description:
Store/replace the push token for one of the caller's devices.

Clients re-POST on every launch and on token rotation. Returns 404 when
the device does not belong to the caller or is revoked (same
anti-enumeration shape as revoke).
Exchange a refresh token for a new access+refresh pair.

Consume a pairing nonce; create or re-register the agent for its owner; push to the WS.

Authenticated as a non-admin user. The successful CAS-consume of the
nonce is the single-flight authority: replays return 410 Gone.
Mint a short code for the operator to retype on the agent host.

Exchange a retyped code for a pairing nonce. Anonymous by necessity.

The agent has no credentials yet — that is the whole point of pairing —
so this endpoint authenticates nothing. It hands back no secret beyond
a nonce that is worthless without the account owner's separate confirm,
plus the masked account name the operator needs to decide whether to
grant this machine to that account at all.

delete.description: Abandon a pairing request and expire any nonce it handed out.

get.description: Poll a minted code. Owner-scoped: a foreign ``request_id`` is a 404.

post.description: Approve a redeemed code and release credentials to the waiting agent.

Allocate a single-use pairing nonce and return its QR payload.

Anonymous: the install scripts and the running agent both call this
before any credentials exist. Replay-resistance comes from the
192-bit nonce + the short TTL + the single-flight CAS at claim time.

get.description:
Report the relay's signing fingerprint and the account's recorded pin.

Advisory only. Clients may display the pair and warn when they differ,
but must not copy ``account_trust_key_fp`` into a local trust store.
List the caller's non-deleted saved shortcuts (all session kinds).

schema.title: Response List Shortcuts Api Shortcuts Get

post.description:
Upsert: re-saving an existing (kind, chord_token) updates its name
instead of duplicating the button; the status stays 201 on both paths.

get.description: List the caller's non-deleted prompt templates.

schema.title: Response List Templates Api Templates Get

delete.description:
Soft-delete the template. Idempotent: deleting an already-deleted
template still returns 204.

post.description: Bump ``last_used_at`` for picker-tap recents tracking.

get.description:
Return the manifest-signing public key for agent-side bootstrap.

The agent's auto-updater needs this key (pinned at
``<prefix>/trust/central_server.pub``) to verify Ed25519 signatures on
every release manifest. The install scripts and the
``mobaide-agent fetch-trust-key`` CLI fetch this endpoint when the
operator hasn't pre-set ``MOBAIDE_AGENT_TRUST_KEY_B64``. Returns 503
when ``MANIFEST_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY`` is unset on this server — agents
cannot bootstrap auto-update against a server that has no signing key
configured. Anonymous: matches the public ``manifest.json`` contract,
so unpaired install hosts can fetch it before having any credentials.
